name: Eritrea

findings.financier: Export-Import Bank of China (RMB 166m government concessional loan)
findings.summary: Phase 1 of a China Eximbank-financed telecom rehabilitation: ZTE, under a 2005 contract, rehabilitated Eritel's 200,000-line fixed network and rolled out a nationwide CDMA wireless network, completed in June 2009.

sources.publisher: Direction générale du Trésor (French Ministry of Economy)

findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: ZTE is the equipment vendor. US$21.45m is the ZTE contract value per AidData; the RMB 166m loan is not converted. ZTE is named only by AidData; Trésor (2022) and BTW Media (2025) confirm a 2006 Chinese concessional loan for telecom modernisation (both say US$23m) without naming a vendor. Trésor coded S1 as a government publication, but it is a foreign government's country note: reviewer call. Pre-2020: whether the CDMA network is still in service was not confirmed.

findings.financier: Export-Import Bank of China (government concessional loan)
findings.summary: Phase 2 of the Eximbank-financed rehabilitation, with ZTE and Huawei as contractors, was to build Eritel a national MPLS IP backbone, a GSM mobile network and the TSEiNET ISP network; AidData records it completed in 2014.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: equipment vendors ZTE and Huawei; the split between them is not documented. Tier 4 not 5: AidData marks the project complete (2012-2014) but gives no operational detail. US$23m is AidData's single-source estimated face value; it matches the figure Trésor and BTW Media attach to the 2006 loan, so the amounts may be conflated. Pre-2020; current status not confirmed, though Eritel remains the sole operator and plausibly still runs this kit.
